correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation supplies the exact p-norm Hessian as a weighted least-squares minimum. Dimensional p-versus-2 estimates yield F_p-cE convex for 1<p<2 and CE-F_p convex for p>2 (coordinate-zero and origin boundaries checked by line restriction). Their convexity gives global two-sided triangular-defect comparability for equal sub-Hilbert exponent and all Euclidean-regularized super-Hilbert exponents. Taylor expansion at (e1,e1+t e2) proves the distinct exact leading powers and exhausts necessity for every p,q,a,b in range. The exact defect ratio supremum b/a and the source metric formula establish two-sided log distance and coefficient one. Finite deterministic checks passed and are treated as diagnostics only.

value.rationale: The motivating new norm-cone metric has few natural non-Hilbert families classified. This result completely partitions a continuous two-parameter family of smooth strictly convex norms into intrinsic parts, identifies an asymmetric threshold at p=2 under natural additive Hilbert regularization, and quantifies unbounded intrinsic distance under vanishing ordinary norm perturbations. These answer a structural geometry question, beyond reproducing the motivating ell_2/ell_4 special case.
